get.description: Retrieves a list of all available permission level options within a company. The `id` field in the response represents the UUID to be used for `permission_level_id` in API calls related to user permissions.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description:
Unique identifier for the company. This parameter accepts both formats:
- **Recommended**: Procore company ID (integer) - Use this for new integrations
- Legacy: LaborChart UUID format (uuid string) - Supported for backward compatibility

A proxy layer automatically handles both formats, but using the Procore company ID is preferred for consistency with other Procore APIs.

schema.description: Returns an array of available permission level options.

items.description: Object representing an available permission level option.

id.description: Unique identifier for the permission level.

name.description: The name of the permission level.

error.description: If you receive a 401 error, please ensure you are following the OAuth 2.0 guidelines outlined at https://developers.procore.com/documentation/introduction and verify you can successfully call the /me endpoint using your access token. Additionally, the user associated with that token must be added as a user in the Workforce Planning People List for the corresponding company.

x-changelog.description:
These endpoints have been made available through the
Procore Rest API (https://api.procore.com) now. Their
legacy documentation is still available at
https://wfp-quickconnect.readme.io/docs/getting-started and
will be accessible from https://api-app.laborchart.com
through the end of 2025. This changelog marks the
beginning of their soft deprecation. They will be fully
deprecated in January of 2026 and no longer available
except through the Procore Rest API. They are the same
endpoints and offer full parity. Please begin migrating over at
your earliest convenience.
